name: Identifier
description:
A single word, the one that has no namespace separators in it.

```
 Some\Any::CONST_NAME
           ^^^^^^^^^^ a single word

 Some\Any::BAR*BAZ
           ^^^ ^^^ two single words
```

name: LogicalTypeNode
description:
Several types joined by an operator, like a union or an intersection.

A type of the same kind is flattened into its parent: an `A|(B|C)`
holds the three types side by side.

The flattening and the minimum of two types are checked on creation
only. Since PHP 8.4, property hooks make it possible to keep the checks
permanent.

name: Name
description:
A name: the namespace it begins with and the word it ends in.

```
 Some\Any
 ^^^^     the namespace
      ^^^ the word

 \Some\Any
 ^^^^^     a fully qualified namespace begins in a separator

 \Any
 ^    the root namespace

 non-empty-string
 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ a single word, there is no namespace
```

properties.name: value
properties.description: The last word of the name, it has no separators.

properties.name: namespace
properties.description:
The namespace the word belongs to, or `null` in case of the
name is written with none.

name: NamedTypeNode
description:
A type referenced by name, along with whatever the name is followed by.

The meaning of what follows is left to whoever reads the tree, as it depends
on the type the name stands for. A `FOO` may be a constant or a class, and
the template arguments of an `array{a: int, ...<string, int>}` are not the
ones of an `array<int>`.

```
 Some\Any<int, string>
 ^^^^^^^^              the name
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the template arguments

 array{name: string}
 ^^^^^               the name
      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the shape fields

object{name: string, ...<string, mixed>}
^^^^^^                                   the name
      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the shape fields
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  the template arguments
```

properties.name: arguments
properties.description:
Template arguments of a type, or `null` in case of the name is
followed by none.

The list is never empty.

```
 Some       // null
 Some<int>  // a list of 1 argument
```

properties.name: fields
properties.description:
Shape fields of a type, or `null` in case of the name is
followed by none. An empty list is not the same as a `null`:
A shape may well be written with no fields at all.

```
 array           // null: no shape
 array{}         // an empty list: a shape of no fields
 array{a: int}   // a list of 1 field
```

name: NamespaceName
description:
A namespace a name or a mask of constants belongs to.

```
 Some\Any\Name
 ^^^^^^^^      a qualified namespace

 \Some\Any\Name
 ^^^^^^^^^      a fully qualified namespace begins in a separator

 namespace\Some\Name
 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^      a namespace relative to the current one
```

The class cannot be named `Namespace`, the word is reserved by PHP.

properties.name: value
properties.description:
The words of the namespace with the separators between them and with
no one at the ends. The `namespace` keyword and the leading separator
are not the words.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: From where the namespace is read.

properties.name: offset
properties.description: Token offset defined in the source code.

name: NodesListNode
description:
An ordered list of nodes of one kind, like the arguments of a generic
or the fields of a shape.

name: SymbolNode
description:
A node that stands for a piece of text: an identifier, a name or a variable.

The text of a node is the one it is written with, so a node is told apart
from the others by `toString()` alone.

name: ThisTypeNode
description:
The type of the object a method is called on, written as a `$this`.

```
 callable(): $this
```

It is written the way a variable is, but it is a type. Any other variable
is a `VariableNode` and no type at all.

name: TypeNode
description: A node standing where a type is expected.

name: TypeOffsetAccessTypeNode
description:
The type standing at an offset of another type.

```
 Some\Any[int]
 ^^^^^^^^      the type an offset is taken of
          ^^^  the offset itself
```

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type an offset is taken of.

properties.name: access
properties.description: The type standing in the square brackets.

name: VariableNode
description:
A variable, written as a name with a `$` in front of it.

```
 callable(int $value): void
 //           ^^^^^^ names a parameter

 ($value is int ? string : bool)
 //^^^^^ stands as the subject of a condition
```

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the variable, written without the leading `$`.

name: WrappingTypeNode
description:
A type built around another one.

```
 ?Some\Any
 ^         the wrapping type
  ^^^^^^^^ the type it wraps
```

name: CallableParameterListNode
CallableParameterNode
description:
A single parameter of a callable.

```
 callable(int &$byRef, string ...$rest, bool $flag = true)
 //       ^^^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 //       by reference  variadic         optional, with a default
```

A parameter is optional when it has a `DefaultValueNode`, with a value
or without one.

The constructor checks the parameter on creation only. The properties are
public and writable, so a later change is not checked. Since PHP 8.4,
property hooks make it possible to keep the checks permanent.

properties.name: type
properties.description:
Type of parameter, or `null` in case of a parameter that is
built by hand and carries a name alone.

properties.name: name
properties.description:
Name of a parameter, or `null` in case of it is written
without one.

```
 callable(int)          // null
 callable(int $value)   // a name
```

properties.name: isByReference
properties.description:
Whether a parameter is taken by reference.

It is written as an `&` behind the type, like the one of
a `callable(int &$byRef)`.

properties.name: isVariadic
properties.description:
Whether a parameter takes every argument left, written as a `...`:
A `callable(string ...$rest)`.

properties.name: default
properties.description:
Default of a parameter, or `null` in case of a required one.
A variadic parameter is optional itself, so it has no default.

```
 callable(int $a)            // null
 callable(int $a =)          // a default without a value
 callable(int $a = 42)       // a default with a value
```

name: CallableTypeNode
description:
Something callable, written as a name with a parameter list behind it.

```
 Closure<T of Some>(T, string ...$rest): T
 ^^^^^^^                                    the name
        ^^^^^^^^^^^                         the template parameters
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^     the parameters
                                         ^  the return type
```

properties.name: parameters
properties.description:
Parameters a callable accepts. The list is never `null`, an
empty list stands for empty parentheses.

```
 callable()      // an empty list
 callable(int)   // a list of 1 parameter
```

properties.name: type
properties.description:
A return type of callable, or `null` in case of it is left
unsaid.

```
 callable()       // null
 callable(): int  // a type
```

properties.name: templates
properties.description:
Template parameters a callable declares, or `null` in case of
it declares none.

The list is never empty.

```
 callable(T): T     // null
 callable<T>(T): T  // a list of 1 parameter
```

name: DefaultValueNode
description:
The default of a callable parameter, written as an `=` and the value it
stands for.

The node itself tells that the parameter may be left out, so a parameter
with it is optional, and one without it is required.

```
 callable(int $a =, string $b = 'x')
 //             ^                      no value, the parameter is optional
 //                            ^^^^^^^ the value
```

properties.name: value
properties.description:
The value of a default, or `null` in case of the parameter
is only marked as optional.

The value is a literal or a constant, so it is a type node of the
same kind as in any other position.

name: ConditionNode

properties.name: kind
properties.description: The kind of the operator between the sides.

name: ConditionKind
description: The kind of a condition, it is the operator the condition is written with.

cases.name: Equal
cases.description:
Whether the subject is the target.

```
 ($value is int ? string : bool)
```

cases.name: NotEqual
cases.description:
Whether the subject is anything but the target.

```
 ($value is not int ? string : bool)
```

name: ConditionalTypeNode
description:
A type chosen by a condition.

```
 ($value is int ? string : bool)
  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^                  the condition
                  ^^^^^^         the type it holds for
                           ^^^^  the type it does not
```

name: ConstMaskTypeNode
description:
A set of constants, referenced by a name written in part.

```
 Some\Any::SOME_*
 ^^^^^^^^         the class the constants belong to
           ^^^^^^ the mask their names are written as

 Some\Any\SOME_*
 ^^^^^^^^        the namespace the constants belong to

 *_SOME
 ^^^^^^ a mask with no class and no namespace at all

 \SOME_*
 ^       a mask of the root namespace
```

A name written whole stands for a single constant, see the
`ConstTypeNode`.

properties.name: owner
properties.description:
The class or the namespace the constants belong to, or
`null` in case of the mask is written with neither.

```
 Some\Any::SOME_*  // the class Some\Any
 Some\Any\SOME_*   // the namespace Some\Any
 \SOME_*           // the root namespace
 SOME_*            // null
```

properties.name: mask
properties.description: The name of the constants, written in part.

name: ConstTypeNode
description:
A single constant, referenced by its whole name.

```
 Some\Any::CONST_NAME
 ^^^^^^^^             the class the constant belongs to
           ^^^^^^^^^^ the name of the constant
```

A name written in part stands for a set of constants, see the
`ConstMaskTypeNode`.

properties.name: owner
properties.description:
The class or the namespace the constant belongs to.

A constant of a namespace written by its whole name
(`Some\CONST_NAME`) is a name of a type in the source, so the
parser builds it as a `NamedTypeNode`.

name: MaskNode
WildcardMaskNode
description:
An asterisk standing in the place of any run of characters of a constant name.

```
 Some\Any::CONST_*
 //              ^ the part of the name that is left unsaid
```

name: BoolLiteralNode
description:
A `true` or a `false`, in any case they are written in.

```
 TruE  // value: true, raw: "TruE"
```

name: FloatLiteralNode
description:
A floating point number.

The value is the nearest double, the mantissa and the exponent keep the
exact number: `mantissa * 10 ** exponent`. A parser stores the nearest bound
of the range (`PHP_FLOAT_MAX`) for a number out of it, never an infinity.

```
 -1_5.5e+3  // value: -15500.0, mantissa: "-15.5", exponent: "3"
 .42        // value: 0.42,     mantissa: "0.42",  exponent: "0"
 - 1.5      // value: -1.5,     mantissa: "-1.5",  exponent: "0"

 // raw: the text as written, "-1_5.5e+3", ".42", "- 1.5"
```

A node made by hand has no text to read the exact number from, so the
mantissa and the exponent are the ones of the value itself.

properties.name: mantissa
properties.description:
The number before the exponent, without separators and leading zeros. The
integer part is always there, the point is there only with a fraction:
`0.5`, `1`, `-0.10`.

properties.name: exponent
properties.description: The power of ten, `0` if there is no exponent.

name: IntLiteralNode
description:
A whole number, written in any of the four radixes.

```
 0xFE_DE  // value: 65246, raw: "0xFE_DE", decimal: "65246", kind: Hexadecimal
 042      // value: 34,    raw: "042",     decimal: "34",    kind: Octal
```

properties.name: decimal
properties.description: The value written out in base 10.

name: LiteralNode
description:
A value standing where a type is expected, kept both as PHP sees it
and as it is written.

The two are not the same thing. A value is what PHP would compute, while
a raw is the very text it was computed from, quotes, radix and all.

```
 0x1F     // value: 31,     raw: "0x1F"
 '\x41'   // value: "\x41", raw: "'\x41'"
```

name: NullLiteralNode
description:
A `null`, in any case it is written in.

```
 NulL  // value: null, raw: "NulL"
```

name: StringLiteralNode
description:
A string, kept both decoded and as it is written.

```
 "\x41\x42"  // value: "AB", raw: "\"\x41\x42\""
```

name: IntersectionTypeNode
description:
All of several types at once.

```
 Some\Any & Stringable
```

name: UnionTypeNode
description:
Any one of several types.

```
 int|string|null
```

name: NamespaceKind
description: How the namespace of a name is written, that is, from where it is read.

cases.name: Qualified
cases.description:
A namespace written as it is.

```
 Some\Any\Name
 ^^^^^^^^
```

cases.name: FullyQualified
cases.description:
A namespace that begins in a separator, it is read from the root.

```
 \Some\Any\Name
 ^^^^^^^^^

 \Name
 ^     the root namespace has no words
```

cases.name: NamespaceRelative
cases.description:
A namespace that begins in the `namespace` keyword, it is read from
the current one. The keyword is not a word of the namespace.

```
 namespace\Some\Name
 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

 namespace\Name
 ^^^^^^^^^      the current namespace has no words
```

name: ComplexFieldNode
ExplicitFieldNode
description:
A field of a shape written with a key of its own.

What the key may be is what tells the children of this class apart.
A `NamedFieldNode` carries a bare word, a `ScalarFieldNode`
a scalar value and a `ComplexFieldNode` a reference that has to
be read.

properties.name: key
properties.description: The key a field is written with.

properties.name: isOptional
properties.description:
Whether a field may be absent, written as a `?` in front of
the colon. Only a field with a key can be marked so.

```
 array{name: string}   // false
 array{name?: string}  // true
```

name: FieldListNode
description:
The fields of a shape, in the order they are written in.

An empty list is a shape written with no fields at all, which is a thing
of its own.

An `array` carries no list, while an `array{}` carries an empty one.
See the `NamedTypeNode::$fields`.

properties.name: isSealed
properties.description:
Whether the shape is written with the fields it lists and no other.
An unsealed one ends in a `...`, which says that whatever else it
carries was left unsaid.

```
 array{a: int}       // sealed
 array{a: int, ...}  // unsealed
```

name: FieldNode
description:
A single field of a shape.

A field is written either with a key or with none, and a shape may mix
the two. The keyless ones are numbered from zero in the order they are
written in.

```
 array{name: string, id: int}  // fields written with a key
 array{string, int}            // fields written with none
 array{string, id: int}        // both in one shape
```

name: ImplicitFieldNode
NamedFieldNode
description:
A field of a shape keyed by a bare word.

```
 array{name: string}
 //    ^^^^ the key
```

A `true`, a `false` and a `null` are bare words as well. In the place of
a key they name nothing but themselves.

name: ScalarFieldNode
TemplateArgumentNode
description:
A value passed to a template parameter, as opposed to a parameter
declared by a type.

```
 Some\Any<int, covariant string, *>
 //       ^^^  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  ^ three arguments
```

name: TemplateBoundNode
description:
One end a template parameter is bounded at, written as the word it is
bounded with and the type the bound is expressed by.

```
 callable<T of Some super Any>(T): T
 //         ^^^^^^^                  the upper bound
 //                 ^^^^^^^^^        the lower bound
```

properties.name: operator
properties.description:
The word the bound is written with: `of` and `as` bound from
above, `super` from below.

name: TemplateListNode
description:
Template arguments a type is referenced with, in the order they are
written in. A slot of the list may also declare a parameter in place of
passing an argument.

The list is never empty.

```
 Some\Any<int, string>
 //       ^^^  ^^^^^^ two arguments
```

name: TemplateNode
description:
Whatever stands in a slot of the `<...>` list of a type: an argument that
is passed or a parameter that is declared right there.

```
 Some\Any<int, *>
 //       ^^^  ^ two arguments

 callable<T of Some>(T): T
 //       ^^^^^^^^^ a parameter
```

name: TemplateParameterListNode
description:
Template parameters a type declares, in the order they are written in.

The list is never empty: a type that declares no parameters carries no
list at all.

```
 callable<T, U of Some>(T): U
 //       ^  ^^^^^^^^^
 //       two parameters
```

name: TemplateParameterNode

properties.name: upper
properties.description:
The end the parameter is bounded at from above, written with an
`of` or an `as`.

The argument is to be a subtype of it.

properties.name: lower
properties.description:
The end the parameter is bounded at from below, written with
a `super`.

The argument is to be a supertype of it.

properties.name: default
properties.description:
The type the parameter takes when no argument is passed, written
with an `=`.

It bounds nothing. A bound says what an argument may be, while
a default says what it becomes when left unsaid.

properties.name: variance
properties.description:
Declaration-site variance of the parameter, or `null` in case of
it carries none, which makes the parameter invariant.

name: TypedTemplateArgumentNode
description:
A template argument that is a type, along with the call-site variance it
may carry.

```
 Some\Any<int, covariant string>
 //       ^^^                    an invariant argument
 //            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  a covariant argument
```

properties.name: variance
properties.description:
Variance standing in front of the argument, or `null` in case of
it carries none, which makes the argument invariant.

```
 Some\Any<covariant string>
 //       ^^^^^^^^^ the variance
```

name: VarianceNode
description:
A variance of a template argument or of a template parameter, the word that
stands in front of it.

```
 Some\Any<covariant string>
 //       ^^^^^^^^^ the variance

 callable<contravariant T>(T): void
 //       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the variance
```

properties.name: kind
properties.description: The kind of the variance.

name: VarianceKind
description: The kind of a variance, it is the word the variance is written with.

cases.name: Covariant
cases.description:
A subtype may stand in the place of the type.

```
 Some\Any<covariant string>
```

cases.name: Contravariant
cases.description:
A supertype may stand in the place of the type.

```
 Some\Any<contravariant string>
```

cases.name: Invariant
cases.description:
Only the type itself may stand in its place.

```
 Some\Any<invariant string>
```

name: WildcardTemplateArgumentNode
description:
A template argument that is left unsaid, written as an asterisk.

```
 Some\Any<*>
 //       ^ an unspecified argument
```

The node names no type and carries no variance.

name: NullableTypeNode
description:
A type a `null` is allowed besides, written with a leading `?`.

```
 ?Some\Any
```

name: TypesListTypeNode
description:
A list of the wrapped type, written in the legacy `[]` notation.

```
 Some\Any[]
 ^^^^^^^^   the type the list is made of

 Some\Any[][]
 ^^^^^^^^^^   a list the outer list is made of
```
